launcher_icon._doc: The launcher icon, generated from this declaration by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-launcher-icons.py (pattern + category colours + glyphs in 1_cicd/src/data/launcher-icons.json). Never edit the generated res files.

name: cloud-dialer
_doc_vendored_engine: CI does NOT run the engine source in 1_cicd/src/scripts — it runs the VENDORED COPY at ./build.sh, from this directory. This key DECLARES that copy relationship so the workflow generator can enforce byte-identity (cloud-android-ship-repo-workflow-engine.sh, step 'verify engine ↔ vendored build.sh parity') and go red on drift. Editing the engine alone used to change nothing at ship time, silently — which is how the ABI gate and the GHCR auto-delete gate came to exist only in the file nobody executes. Re-sync with: cp 1_cicd/src/scripts/<engine> ./build.sh

dialer.tracker_dir_note: flattened 2026-08-29 — the vendored source now sits at the app root, matching every other app in this repo instead of hiding under upstream/. upstream_repo/pinned_tag stay provenance only; bump pinned_tag + re-run materialize-fork to re-vendor a newer upstream tag.

call_screening._doc: Owner contract for the CallScreeningService patches (0007/0012/0013). default_mode MUST equal the code's first-run seed (App.onCreate). Patch 0013 adds the screened-call history + per-number allowlist (allowed numbers always ring, overriding every mode).
call_screening.rationale: spam/robocall defence by default; saved contacts ring normally, everything else is silently rejected and logged to the in-app screened-call history

build._doc: Fossify Phone. gradle task + keystore signing. 1.11.1 has productFlavors {core,foss,gplay} (dimension 'variants') — build ONLY the foss flavor (no GMS; the fork self-updates via GHCR) and glob its flavored output dir. CI 32144280344 proved assembleRelease builds all 3 flavors and the flavorless apk/release/ glob matches nothing.

gradle_props._doc: -P props patch 0005/0006 read. APPLICATION_ID is MANDATORY — without it the APK builds as stock org.fossify.phone and identity-assert refuses to publish (CI 32145181294). Updater props have safe in-repo defaults; we enable auto-update explicitly (fleet updater is the point of the fork).

modules._doc: Shared modules settings.gradle.kts includes BY REFERENCE. Declared so the ship workflow watches them and the publish gate hashes them: a change to any of them must rebuild the dialer, not ride along unshipped. settings.gradle.kts still names them as literals (upstream's file, not a loop over this map).

libs:core._doc_dir: Fleet mesh membership: core manifest-merges the CONSTELLATION_DATA signature permission.

libs:devtools._doc_dir: Pulled in by core's `api project(':libs:devtools')` (FleetTokenProvider, FleetMemberReceiver, MESH_MEMBER <queries>); not linked directly.

libs:ui-kit._doc: 2026-10-16 owner decision: all apps must be Compose. Shared BY REFERENCE: the fleet's Compose kit (CloudKitTheme + KitPalette) ScreeningLogActivity and CallProviderChooserSheet paint with.

libs:crash._doc: #1122 libs:core `api`s this module (the default crash handler, the local crash sink and the generic crash screen); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:fleetconfig-model._doc: #873 libs:core `api`s this module (the setup provider every app serves, describe / export / apply / status); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:bottomnav._doc: #868 NavDecl and the scaffold the shared nav libs build on, with the SMS section. Shared BY REFERENCE; build.json::ui declares what it shows.

libs:ui-icons._doc: #1160 the nav icon catalog (name to ImageVector, tinted or brand): every nav glyph of every app, shared BY REFERENCE; libs:bottomnav depends on it.

libs:ui-nav-bars._doc: #1164 shared navigation and theme design, shared BY REFERENCE.

libs:perms._doc: #1360 the permission contract (libs:perms): Configs > General > Perms (AppPermsSection, linked by libs:ui-nav-bars), first run (PermsFirstRun), PermsGate, and the state provider helper apps are read through.

libs:theme-background._doc: #1164 shared navigation and theme design, shared BY REFERENCE.

web._doc: #876 Cloud Dialer as a Kotlin/Wasm page (web/ is its own gradle root; the shared libs' pure-Compose sources arrive through the ab_cloud-libs-shared/web composite). Rendered into 1_cicd/src/cicd/ship-cloud-dialer-wasm.yml by the workflow generator: `./gradlew wasmJsBrowserDistribution` in `dir`, tested by test/test-dialer-web.sh, `build/dist/wasmJs/productionExecutable` zipped to `artifact` and attached to the rolling release as `gh_asset`. A mocked page: the island and tab strips are ui.bottom_nav / ui.sections as the Android shell reads them, the first section shows mock data and the rest say they live in the Android app. The APK's own ship ignores this directory.

tests._doc: Read by 1_cicd/dist/scripts/cloud-android-test-engine.sh, which the ship workflow runs before it builds. shell = test/test-*.sh (static assertions incl. test-no-fake-app-check.sh and the SMS role/nav testers); unit = the JVM suites in app/src/test (foss flavor, the only one we ship).

gh_release._doc: Rolling GH release 'latest' (shared across the ea_cloud-* apps; each contributes a distinctly-named APK asset), overwritten every main push so https://github.com/diegonmarcos/cloudy-u-android/releases/latest/download/cloud-comms-dialer.apk stays stable. Published by `build.sh gh-release-fork dialer` (ship-cloud-dialer.yml), which uploads dist/cloud-comms-dialer.apk with --clobber. Consumed by aa_cloud-superapp ui.external_apps[cloud-dialer].install_apk_url. The immutable timestamped per-build release (RSS notification) is separate and stays --latest=false.

analytics._doc: Consumed by :libs:analytics, which reads THIS file (rootDir) at build time and bakes the values into BuildConfig. Both backends are single-site today, so every app reports into the same site and is told apart by .app — give each app its own site_id once per-app sites exist in Umami/Matomo.

ui._doc: #868 THE navigation declaration (libs:bottomnav's NavDecl): ui.bottom_nav is the island's section ids in display order, ui.sections[] each carry the one page they show. Home, Contacts, Favorites and Calls are the upstream pager pages; Settings > Manage shown tabs still hides the three optional ones. SMS is the default-SMS-app screen. app/build.gradle.kts bakes this as UI_SECTIONS_B64 / UI_BOTTOM_NAV / UI_DEFAULT_SECTION.

configs_pages._doc: Configs > General and Configs > About (libs:ui-nav-bars fleetconfigs, rule 1_cicd/src/data/configs-pages.json). general.sections: the anchors and sections of the one General page, in order (perms, battery, storage, notifications, ui, language are required; app opens this app's own Configs). about: what the app does, its features, privacy and the fleet services it talks to (ids of ac_cloud-account/build.json::fleet_endpoints, resolved to mesh URLs at build time). Name, icon, version, build sha, repo, licence, crash sink and debug API are derived, never typed here.

about.what: The phone's dialer and messages app: calls, contacts, favourites and SMS.
about.privacy: No ads and no third-party trackers. A crash report is saved on the phone and sent only to the phone's own C3 WebServer over loopback; nothing leaves the device unless you share it. Usage analytics are opt-in and off by default; when allowed, events go only to the owner's self-hosted Umami and Matomo. It calls no fleet service: its data stays on the phone.

perms._doc: #1360 every grant this app needs, by libs:perms catalogue id (needs), and the fleet apps that do work for it with the grants THEY must hold (helpers). The ONE declaration: generated into assets/app-perms.json (cloud-android-perms-guard.py --write), drawn by Configs > General > Perms (libs:perms AppPermsSection) with live state, Grant / Open and Grant all, asked at first run (first_run), and reported as 'Missing permission X - Grant' when an operation fails (PermsGate). perms-guard fails when code uses a gated API or another app's engine that is not declared here, or when the manifest and this list disagree.
